cim: A series about artificial intelligence destroying humanity is being filmed
cim_eredeti: A series about artificial intelligence destroying humanity is being filmed
szoveg_eredeti:
Ron Howard of Imagine Entertainment has been hired to direct the pilot, while Akiva Goldsman of Weed Road will serve as showrunner and writer of the pilot.

According to US media, Imagine Entertainment and Weed Road are developing a "Robopocalypse" series based on the 2011 book by Daniel H. Wilson.

Ron Howard of Imagine Entertainment has been hired to direct the pilot, while Akiva Goldsman of Weed Road will serve as showrunner and writer for the pilot. No television network or streaming service has been attached yet.

The book gained widespread fame in the early 2010s when Steven Spielberg bought it to direct before it was published, with a draft script written by Drew Goddard. Spielberg had been toying with the idea of ​​a film adaptation for years, with Anne Hathaway and Chris Hemsworth being considered for the lead roles. Spielberg finally shelved the project indefinitely in 2014, with Michael Bay joining the team as director in 2018. That version was also not filmed. Spielberg's Amblin Entertainment will now executive produce the series. Brian Grazer and Jeb Brody, as well as Greg Lesance and Rachel Wiesenberg, will lead development alongside Goldsman and Howard.

The novel is more relevant than ever amid current fears about artificial intelligence that could bring about the downfall of humanity. The plot focuses on humanity's war against robots controlled by powerful artificial intelligence, and according to the synopsis:

"In the near future, the dazzling technology that powers our world turns against us. At Zero Hour - the moment the robots strike - the human race is nearly destroyed, but as its scattered remnants regroup, humanity unites for the first time in a determined fight to fight back. Brilliantly conceived and incredibly detailed, 'Robopocalypse' is an action epic with ominous implications about the real-world technology that surrounds us."

"'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and tension of a big action story, but what appealed to me was the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its core," Howard said in an official statement.

"Daniel has created a future that feels both startling and increasingly compelling, with characters who must figure out what connects us when the technology we rely on turns against us. I'm also thrilled to be working with Akiva again. We've had some incredibly meaningful creative experiences and this feels like the right story to bring us back together," he added.

Howard and Goldsman have been longtime collaborators, ever since the film "A Beautiful Mind," which earned Howard Oscars for Best Director and Best Picture, while Goldsman won for Best Adapted Screenplay.

They also had a huge hit with "The Da Vinci Code," their adaptation of Dan Brown's novel. The 2006 film grossed over $760 million worldwide.
